candidates.name: Adverse possession of registered land (PG4) collection
verified_facts: Last updated 2 February 2026.
The guide covers applications for adverse possession of registered land.
semantic_limits: Adverse-possession procedure is legal/title evidence, not terrain measurement.

candidates.name: Practice guide 4: adverse possession of registered land
verified_facts: Ordinary title plans show general boundaries unless determined under section 60.
Land may legally fall inside or outside red edging contrary to a simplistic plan reading.
Where the issue is plan accuracy rather than adverse possession, alteration procedures may be appropriate.
semantic_limits: Red edging cannot be converted into an exact parcel line for terrain sampling.

candidates.name: Practice guide 5: historic/unregistered adverse possession
verified_facts: Updated 1 June 2026.
The guide states that red edging does not define the precise legal boundary under the general-boundaries rule.
Register alteration or determined-boundary procedures may be relevant where plan accuracy is the issue.
semantic_limits: Historic possession/title procedure is not elevation evidence.

candidates.name: Adverse possession registration form ADV1
verified_facts: ADV1 is the official application form for registration of a person in adverse possession.
It is an application workflow artifact rather than a spatial measurement product.
semantic_limits: Application form status cannot validate parcel geometry or height.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - where to view LiDAR data
verified_facts: The WMS Preview is an image of LiDAR data.
The preview cannot be queried.
Coverage Metadata Files preview shows raster extents rather than the raster values themselves.
semantic_limits: Preview imagery and footprint views are excluded from numeric sampling.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - finding available data in an AOI
verified_facts: Updated 17 September 2024.
EA directs users to Survey Index Catalogues to determine data availability for an area of interest.
If no data is listed, EA states the location has not been surveyed to date.
semantic_limits: Catalogue presence proves availability/lineage, not the sampled height result.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR data metadata
verified_facts: Updated 5 February 2024.
EA says index catalogues can be downloaded for all products.
The catalogues include details on the time of year data was collected.
semantic_limits: Tile/survey lineage must be obtained from the catalogue; it is not inferred from composite publication date.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - current LiDAR capture programme
verified_facts: EA provides a capture-programme web application.
It includes a forward look and previous captured seasons.
semantic_limits: Capture-programme status does not prove which survey supplied a composite parcel cell.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR survey schedule
verified_facts: EA publishes a survey programme and directs users to the Capture Programme for current/planned progress.
semantic_limits: A planned or captured season is not substituted for the actual survey-index lineage used by the composite.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Esri shapefile technical specification
verified_facts: OS describes shapefile as a simple non-topological geometry/attribute format.
Terrain 5 contour and spot-height shapefiles include a projection file and per-tile metadata.
semantic_limits: File format/topology characteristics do not improve terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 GML feature types
verified_facts: Contour lines, spot heights and land-water boundaries are distinct feature types.
SpotHeight propertyValue is a z value above Newlyn or another British height datum.
Contour/tideline coordinates are rounded to two decimal places.
semantic_limits: Vector contour/spot-height attributes remain secondary evidence, not primary parcel raster samples.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product glossary
verified_facts: OS explicitly defines resolution as discrimination ability with no implication as to accuracy.
A dataset may have fine coordinate rounding while substantially worse accuracy.
semantic_limits: Stored precision/resolution must never be promoted to measurement accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 data structure
verified_facts: In permanent tidal water, mean-low-water height can be extended to the tile edge.
Foreshore heights are interpolated between mean-high-water and mean-low-water heights.
Contours are delivered as polyline and spot-height features.
semantic_limits: Interpolated foreshore behaviour is source modelling, not parcel-specific observed ground truth.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product supply
verified_facts: Terrain 5 is supplied as 5 km by 5 km tiles.
Quarterly supplies incorporate updates from the revision programme.
Product supply is a full-tile resupply rather than a parcel-level acquisition timestamp.
semantic_limits: Quarterly publication cannot be used as a parcel flying date.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 contour data specification
verified_facts: Contour GML follows GML 3.2.1 simple features level 0.
Spot heights are selected by an automated process.
Spot-height z values are rounded to one decimal place and genuine depressions may occur.
semantic_limits: Automated/rounded spot heights cannot replace primary DTM raster sampling.

candidates.name: OpenGIS Web Coverage Service 1.0.0 (deprecated)
verified_facts: OGC lists document 05-076 as deprecated WCS 1.0.0.
The specification distinguishes WCS coverage data from rendered WMS pictures.
Changing grid resolution or response CRS can require interpolation; the INTERPOLATION parameter controls resampling method where supported.
semantic_limits: Deprecated WCS behaviour is version-lineage evidence only; current implementation contracts take precedence.

candidates.name: GML in JPEG 2000 (GMLJP2) 2.0 Core
verified_facts: GMLJP2 2.0 is an approved OGC standard for geospatial raster/grid encoding.
Rectified-grid coverages require an associated CRS.
For a grid point representing a sample space such as an image pixel, the grid point represents the centre of the sample space.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre encoding semantics do not establish source elevation accuracy.

candidates.name: GML Application Schema Coverages JPEG2000 Coverage Encoding Extension
verified_facts: The standard requires coverage axis ordering to follow the declared CRS.
Raster-space bounds must respect whether cell geometry is point/centre or area.
Multi-component range ordering must match the declared range type.
semantic_limits: Encoding conformance cannot substitute for authoritative terrain-source lineage or RMSE.
